newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks rally at opening to year highs.
newsitem.headline: French stocks rally at opening to year highs.

text.p: French stocks rallied in early trading on Tuesday as a stronger dollar and surging bond markets drove the bourse to its highest levels this year.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 28.45 points, or 1.23 percent, at 2,347.08 at 0915 GMT, within striking distance of its all time record 2,360.98 set in February 1994. The CAC-40 December futures contract was 29.5 points higher at 2,351.
"The rise may look excessive but if you look at it objectively, Paris is lagging the other European markets, particularly Frankfurt where the gap is 500 points," a trader said.
Chartists see resistance on the CAC at current levels and at 2,360.
The advance was broadly based, with recent market underperformers leading the move forward, including electrical equipment supplier Schneider, which gained two percent to 249.90 francs.
Blue chips attracted portfolio managers carrying out year-end window-dressing. Luxury goods group LVMH shares gained 2.3 percent to 1,366 francs.

Shares in tyremaker Michelin rose 2.62 percent to 278.50 francs. Brokers report arbitrage between Michelin and other shares in the car sector that weakened on Tuesday on a 22 percent drop in new car sales in France in November.
